title: introduce-slot-pooling-lease-coordinator-and-kv-staleness-watermarks
creator: Aditi Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
The current lease coordinator couples slot allocation, prefetching, and eviction triggers. Under bursty workloads the coordinator oscillates between aggressive eviction and conservative prefetching which produces KV cache thrashing and long tail latencies (~P99+500ms spikes observed). Additionally, the coordinator's lock-heavy path is a hotspot during continuous-batching commit phases, increasing CPU contention.

Proposal summary:
Replace the monolithic lease coordinator with a slot-pooling model and an independent KV staleness watermarking service. The slot pool holds reusable execution slots sized to common batch shapes, reducing allocate/free churn. The watermarking service estimates per-shard KV freshness and surfaces a non-blocking eviction recommendation stream instead of sync eviction calls. Components communicate over a light event bus (in-memory queue with backpressure) so the main scheduler fast-path is lock-free.

Goals:
- Reduce P99 generation latency by at least 10-15% on synthetic chat workloads with mixed seq lengths.
- Eliminate eviction-induced latency spikes and reduce observed eviction storms by 20% in stress tests.
- Reduce coordinator lock contention and CPU sys-time during 95-99th percentile load.
- Provide an incremental feature-flagged rollout path with observability hooks.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Slot pooling increases resident memory for pooled slot state; we mitigate with adaptive pool sizing based on recent footprint histograms.
- Watermarking uses a probabilistic freshness estimator (bloom-filter-like sketch) per KV shard to avoid heavy scans; this may occasionally over-approximate "stale" entries but never under-approximates. That design favors safety (fewer false negatives) at the cost of slightly higher eviction recommendations.
- Decoupling eviction into an async advisory stream simplifies the fast-path but requires careful backpressure to avoid queueing large eviction backlogs. We'll implement queue length-based hysteresis and a bounded worker pool for actual eviction jobs.
- Compatibility wrapper: we implement a thin adapter so legacy components that call the old coordinator API are forwarded to the slot pool/watermark service. This reduces rollout risk but adds temporary translation overhead.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype slot pool with deterministic slot recycling and unit tests (local iteration).
2) Implement watermark estimator and advisory stream; expose metrics: watermark_age_ms, advisory_queue_len, evict_job_latency.
3) Replace coordinator fast-path to borrow slots and emit advisory events (feature flag).
4) Add bounded eviction worker pool and hysteresis policy for draining advisory queues.
5) Compatibility adapter and integration tests with continuous-batching harness.
6) Load tests and canary rollout with telemetry checks before wide release.

Acceptance criteria and observability:
- Unit and integration tests covering pool lifecycle, watermark accuracy bounds, and adapter semantics.
- Benchmark: P99 generation latency improvement >= 10% on standard replay trace and <5% mem increase on 90% of runs.
- Eviction storms metric (evictions_per_minute_on_spike) decreased by >=20% in synthetic eviction stress test.
- No regression in correctness for KV reads/writes: validate via end-to-end fuzzer and golden trace.
- Feature flag exists and circuit-breaker will revert to legacy coordinator automatically if advisory queue > threshold for 2 consecutive minutes.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (canary): runtime-1.24/canary in one region with 5% traffic, monitor watermark_age_ms and eviction queue length.
- Stage 2 (ramp): 25% traffic with extended load tests overnight.
- Stage 3 (full): 100% with 48h observation window.

Why this is different from recent work:
Previous tickets addressed batching windows, eviction tuning, and sharding of KV. This ticket focuses on reorganizing the coordinator into composable pieces (slot pool + advisory watermarking) with the goal of simplifying the scheduler fast-path and preventing eviction-driven P99 spikes rather than incremental tuning of eviction heuristics.
